title: Sign up and log in
description: How to sign up for WHITEBOARD for the first time and how to log in — with Google, Apple, or email and password
headings: Sign up for the first time
Log in with Google or Apple
Or log in with email and password
text: In this guide you'll sign up for WHITEBOARD and log in for the first time. You can sign in with your Google or Apple account in one click, or with email and password — whatever works for you. 1 Open the login screen Go to the platform's login URL and you'll land on the WHITEBOARD login screen. The WHITEBOARD sign-in screen — sign in with Google, Apple, or email 2 Sign up for the first time Don't have an account yet? Click Sign up here at the bottom of the card. Signing up creates an account on the Trial plan — ₪0 forever, no credit card required. Pro tip Not sure which plan is right for you? Start free and upgrade when you need to. Full details in the WHITEBOARD plans guide. 3 Log in with Google or Apple The fastest way: click the Google or Apple button at the top of the card, pick your account — and you're in. Heads-up: signing in with Google counts as accepting the Terms of Use. 4 Or log in with email and password Below the "or log in with email" divider, fill in: Email — the email address you signed up with. Password — click the eye icon to show your password as you type. Check the Terms of Use consent box. Click Log in . Sign in with email and password — the Sign In button 5 Forgot your password? Click Forgot password below the password field and follow the reset instructions. Good to know Signed up with Google? You don't have a password on the platform — just keep logging in with Google. What's next You're in? Great. Head to the dashboard tour — your home base on the platform.

title: Get to know the dashboard
description: A guided tour of the instructor dashboard — metrics, BOARDi insights, tasks, activity, and the revenue chart
headings: Get your bearings in the sidebar and top bar
text: The dashboard is the first screen you'll see every time you log in. It brings everything happening today into one place: revenue, students, tasks waiting for you, and BOARDi insights. In this guide we'll walk through it area by area. 1 Open the dashboard In the sidebar, click Dashboard . At the top of the screen you'll get a greeting with a quick snapshot — how many students are active right now and how many tasks are waiting. Next to the greeting are two quick-action buttons: Create new course and Export report . The instructor's dashboard — the greeting, the quick buttons, and the key metrics 2 Read the key metrics Below the greeting sits a strip of four metrics: Revenue today Active students Active courses Course completion rate Each metric comes with a change arrow (green for up, pink for down) versus the previous period — so you can spot trends at a glance. The key-metrics strip — today's revenue, active students, active courses, and completion rate 3 See what BOARDi found The BOARDi Insights panel shows insights BOARDi has pulled from your data: students at risk of dropping off, a course spiking in sales, a lesson students abandon halfway through. Every insight comes with an action button — like Create win-back email — so you can act on it without leaving the screen. The Refresh button asks BOARDi for fresh insights. The BOARDi Insights panel — BOARDi's daily insights with action buttons 4 Review your tasks and activity Two cards sit side by side: What's waiting for you today — tasks that need attention: failed payments, students awaiting approval, club messages, an upcoming live session. Each task has a direct action button. Recent activity — a feed of events: purchases, course completions, club joins, and reviews. The 'What's waiting for you today' and 'Recent activity' cards on the dashboard 5 Dive into the data Further down the screen: Revenue — a chart with range toggles: 7D, 30D, 90D, YTD. Top courses — your courses ranked by revenue, with student counts and star ratings. Stars of the week — your standout students: watch hours, lessons completed, and streak days. Weekly pulse — weekly engagement metrics. 6 Get your bearings in the sidebar and top bar The sidebar is your main navigation: Dashboard , My knowledge hubs , BOARDi , My library , and Settings . At its bottom — the instructor/student mode switch and your profile. In the top bar you'll find the language switcher, the light/dark mode toggle, and a Settings shortcut. Pro tip Want to see your course through a student's eyes? Use the switch at the bottom of the sidebar — details in Switching between instructor mode and student mode . What's next On your first login, the platform offers a guided tour of all these areas — see Built-in guided tours . Ready to build? Create a new course .

title: Switch between instructor mode and student mode
description: How to switch to student mode to see your courses exactly as students see them — and switch back to instructor mode
text: Before you publish a course, it's worth seeing it exactly the way a student will. That's what the switch between instructor mode and student mode is for — no logging out, no second account. 1 Find the mode switch The switch sits at the bottom of the sidebar, under the "View mode" label: two buttons side by side — Student and Instructor . The highlighted button is your current mode. The toggle between student mode and instructor mode at the bottom of the sidebar 2 Switch to student mode Click Student . The platform switches to the student view: the full instructor sidebar is replaced by a narrow, icons-only sidebar, and the menus show what a student sees — their courses, library, and progress. This is the exact same view students get when they log in themselves — not a simulation. Good to know Student mode is built for checking your work: it's how you make sure lessons, locks, and structure look the way you planned — before real students walk in. 3 Switch back to instructor mode On the same switch, click Instructor and you're back in the full management environment — the wide sidebar with all your management tools: dashboard, knowledge hubs, BOARDi, library, and settings. What's next Now that you know how to check the student experience, continue to A tour of the dashboard or launch the built-in guided tours for a walkthrough.

title: The built-in guided tours (Walk Me)
description: The intro tour that runs on your first login, the module guides, and how to relaunch any tour from the "My guides" menu
text: You don't have to read guides to learn the platform — it teaches itself. WHITEBOARD includes built-in guided tours (Walk Me) that walk you through the actual screens, step by step, and you can relaunch them anytime. 1 Take the intro tour On your first login, a 23-stop intro tour opens automatically. It walks you through the main areas — the dashboard, the sidebar, knowledge hubs, and more — with a short explanation of each. Move at your own pace, or exit midway and come back later. 2 Relaunch a tour Missed something, or want a refresher? Click the BOARDi icon in the top bar and choose My guides from the menu. From there you can relaunch the intro tour or any other guide. The actions area in the top bar — this is where the BOARDi icon opens the My Guides menu 3 Use the module guides Beyond the general tour, there are focused guides for each type of knowledge hub: School — setting up your course site Club — building a community around your content Training program — a structured learning path Each guide runs on the module's real screens and shows you where everything lives. Pro tip The guides are most useful the first time you enter a new module — launch the module guide before you start building. What's next Want support beyond the tours? BOARDi answers questions anywhere on the platform. And for a proper overview of the main screen — A tour of the dashboard .

title: Edit your personal profile
description: Updating your profile photo, personal details, bio, social links, and security and notification settings
headings: Write a bio and add links
text: Your personal profile is your face to your students: your photo, professional title, and bio appear on your course and school pages. In this guide we'll go through every part of the "My profile" screen. 1 Open your profile At the bottom of the sidebar, next to your name and photo, click the edit button (pencil icon). The My profile screen opens, with a floating side navigation that jumps you to each section. 2 Change your profile photo In the Profile photo section, click Change photo and pick a file. If you signed up with Google, your photo is imported from there by default. 3 Update your personal details In the Personal details section, update your first name, last name, and phone number. The email field is locked — the account's email address can't be changed. The personal details area in the profile — name, locked email, and phone 4 Write a bio and add links In the Bio section: Professional title — one line that appears under your name. Bio — tell people about yourself, your experience, and what students will learn from you. Social links — Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, TikTok, and Facebook. 5 Set up security and notifications In the Security section you can click Change password and turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) — an extra layer of protection with a one-time code. In the Notifications section you control what reaches you: updates about new students, a weekly email summary, and marketing notifications. 6 Save your changes The save button sits in the top bar and reflects your current state: the moment you touch a field it shows "Unsaved changes", and after you click — "Settings updated". The save button in the profile's top bar — reflects the change state Heads-up At the bottom of the screen is the Delete account section. This is irreversible — all your data, courses, and student records are permanently deleted and can't be recovered. What's next Profile all set? Move on to your global account settings — that's where you set up your brand, domain, and integrations.

title: WHITEBOARD plans — what's included in each plan
description: Comparing the five plans — Trial, Teacher, Educator, Leader, and Enterprise — pricing, student limits, and what's included
headings: Start free with the Trial plan
Know what happens if you cancel
text: WHITEBOARD has five plans, from free forever to a full enterprise solution. In this guide you'll see what each one includes, so you can choose right — and know you can always upgrade later. 1 Start free with the Trial plan The Trial plan costs ₪0 forever and doesn't require a credit card. It includes up to 100 students and 3 courses, with WHITEBOARD branding locked in. It's the way to test the platform on a real course, risk-free. 2 Compare the paid plans Plan Price Students What you get Trial ₪0 forever, no credit card Up to 100 3 courses, WHITEBOARD branding locked Teacher ₪149/month Up to 2,000 Unlimited courses, one course site, CRM, 0% commission, 30 days free Educator (recommended) ₪199/month Up to 25,000 5 course sites, BOARDi course creation, games, custom domain, API Leader ₪399/month Up to 100,000 Unlimited sites, unlimited BOARDi, Whiteboard Studio + Live Enterprise From ₪899/month (contact us) Unlimited SSO, dedicated success manager A few pointers to help you navigate: Teacher — the entry plan for anyone selling a course: unlimited courses, one course site, built-in CRM, and 0% commission on sales, with your first 30 days free. Educator — the recommended plan: adds 5 course sites, course creation with BOARDi, games, a custom domain, and API access. Leader — for anyone running a full brand: unlimited sites and BOARDi, plus the Whiteboard Studio recording studio and Live broadcasts. Enterprise — for organizations: SSO and a dedicated success manager, arranged with the team. 3 Consider annual billing With annual billing, pricing works on a "pay for 10, get 12" basis — you pay for 10 months and get a full year. Pro tip All plans are commitment-free — you can switch plans or cancel at any point. 4 Know what happens if you cancel Even after canceling, your data doesn't disappear: Full CSV export — you can export all your data at any moment. 30-day grace period — after canceling, you have a full month to access your account and download everything. What's next Sign up free via Signing up and logging in . Selling courses? Read up on Payments and payouts .

title: Create a new course
description: How to create a new course in WHITEBOARD — from the first click to a draft course that's ready to build
headings: Get to know the course workspace
The course is saved as a draft
text: A new course in WHITEBOARD starts as an empty draft: give it a name, add a short description, and you get a full workspace — chapter structure, settings, brand kit, and analytics. This guide walks through the whole flow, so within a few minutes you'll have a course ready to fill with content. 1 Open My knowledge hubs In the side menu, click My knowledge hubs . This is home to all your courses, schools, and programs. Your courses live under My courses . 2 Create the course Click the course creation button and choose a new course. 3 Name and describe it The course name is what students see on the course page and in search — pick something clear, focused, and accurate. The short description is a few sentences explaining what the course is about, who it's for, and what students will get out of it. Pro tip You can change the name and description anytime from the course's Settings tab, so don't get stuck polishing the wording now. 4 Get to know the course workspace After creation, the course page opens. At the top you'll see the course name, its status, and the basic stats (students and lessons), and below them a row of tabs that stays with you throughout the course's life: Layout — building the course structure: chapters, lessons, and content. Settings — name, description, URL, pricing, and more. My students — who's enrolled and how they're progressing. Brand kit — the course's colors, fonts, and logo. Email campaigns — emails and communication with your students. Analytics — viewing and progress data. BOARDi — the course's smart assistant. The course page header with the tab bar At any point you can click Preview at the top of the page to see the course from a student's point of view — worth peeking at every so often while you build. 5 The course is saved as a draft A new course is born in Draft status: it's visible only to you, and you can build it at your own pace. Students will see the course only after you publish it — no pressure to finish everything in a day. While you're still in draft, it's worth checking two easy-to-forget things, both in the Settings tab: Course URL — the URL locks after publishing, so now's the time to make sure it's short and clear. Cover image — the image that represents your course on the course page and in search results. Good to know Once a course is published it can't be moved back to Draft status — so it pays to finish building before you publish. Details in Publishing and sharing your course . What the student sees A student entering the course gets the course player: a sidebar with the chapter and lesson list and a personal progress meter, the lesson area in the center, and a bottom bar with Previous , Next , and Mark as complete buttons. Everything you build from here — structure, content, and brand kit — dresses up this template. The course player from the student's perspective — chapters sidebar, lesson, and navigation bar What's next The next step is building the course skeleton — chapters and lessons. Continue to Building your course structure — chapters and lessons .

title: Build your course structure — chapters and lessons
description: Add chapters and lessons, reorder by dragging, and delete — all structure management happens in the course sidebar
text: A course has two levels of structure: chapters, and inside each chapter — lessons. You manage all of it from the course page sidebar, in edit mode. Here's how. 1 Switch to edit mode On the course page, in the corner of the top bar, click Edit mode . The sidebar now shows edit buttons, a drag handle, and an add button for every chapter and lesson. The course page in edit mode — the chapters and lessons sidebar on the right 2 Add a new chapter At the bottom of the chapter list, click Add new chapter and give it a name. Next to the chapter name you'll see the total watch time of the lessons inside it. The Add chapter button at the bottom of the chapter list 3 Add lessons to a chapter Inside each chapter, click Add lesson to chapter . Every lesson gets its own name, content type, and status — Draft or Published — so you can roll out your course gradually, one lesson at a time. 4 Reorder by dragging Grab the drag handle next to the chapter or lesson name and drag it where you want it. You can reorder entire chapters as well as lessons within a chapter. 5 Edit and delete Every chapter and lesson has an edit button (rename) and a delete button. Heads-up Deleting a lesson can't be undone — the system will ask you to confirm first. If you're not sure, leave the lesson in Draft status instead of deleting it. What the student sees Students see the same sidebar — minus the editing tools: the chapter list with watch times, lessons marked "Completed" for anything they've already watched, and a personal progress meter ("1 / 5 lessons") at the top of the sidebar. Draft lessons aren't hidden from the list — they show as "Not available yet". The course page in the student's eyes — personal progress in the chapters sidebar What's next Now that the skeleton is in place, it's time to decide what goes inside each lesson — head to Lesson types .

title: Lesson types in the platform
description: Video, exam, file, game, and embedded website — which type fits which content, and how to spot each one in the sidebar
headings: How it looks in the sidebar
text: Not every lesson is a video. WHITEBOARD supports several lesson types, and each one has its own icon in the course sidebar — so both you and your students can see at a glance what's waiting in each lesson. The lesson types Video lesson — the most common type: a video you upload or record in the studio, alongside text, files, and other blocks. Exam lesson — questions students answer inside the course, to track understanding. File lesson — a lesson built around a file to download or view, like a slide deck or a workbook. Game lesson — an embedded learning game, like a word search or a memory game. Embedded website (iFrame) — a website or external tool embedded inside the lesson, for example an AI tool for practice. Different lesson types in the sidebar — type icon, duration, and status How it looks in the sidebar Next to each lesson in the sidebar you'll see the watch time, the type icon, and the status tag ( Draft or Published ). Lessons the student has finished are marked as completed. Pro tip Mixing types across a chapter — a video followed by a short exam or a game — keeps students engaged and helps the material stick. What the student sees In the student's sidebar, each lesson shows its type icon and watch time — so students know upfront whether a video, an exam, or a game is coming. Video lessons open in the player, exam and game lessons open as an interactive activity, and an embedded website loads right inside the lesson page. What's next Inside every lesson you can build a full content page from blocks — headings, text, images, and more. Continue to Content blocks inside a lesson .

title: Content blocks inside a lesson
description: Build the lesson page from blocks — headings, text, quote, image, CTA button, embed, and attached files
text: A lesson page in WHITEBOARD is built from blocks — content units you add one after another below the video. That's how you build a rich lesson without touching the design: every block is already styled to match your course's brand kit. 1 Open the block picker In edit mode, at the bottom of the lesson content, click Add content block . A picker opens with all the block types. בוחר הבלוקים — כל סוגי בלוקי התוכן לשיעור 2 Choose a block Here are the available blocks: H1 heading — a large heading to open a topic. H2 subheading — a section heading. Body text — a free-form paragraph. Quote — a highlighted quote with its own styling. Divider — a separator line between content sections. CTA button — an action button with a link. Image / GIF — an image, GIF, or media file. Embed / iFrame — embed a website or external tool inside the lesson. 3 Attach files Below the lesson content there's an Attached files card — that's where you add slide decks, spreadsheets, and any file your students need to download. Click Add file , and each file shows its name, type, and a Download button. An attached-files card inside a lesson Good to know Whether students can download files is controlled from the course's Settings tab, with the "Allow content downloads" toggle. What the student sees Students get the assembled lesson page: the video on top, the blocks below it in the order you set, and the attached files card with a Download button next to each file. Everything renders in your brand kit's design — the fonts and colors you chose, without the editing tools. The lesson page as the student sees it — video, blocks, and attached files What's next In most lessons the centerpiece block is the video — continue to Uploading videos to WHITEBOARD storage .

title: Upload videos to WHITEBOARD storage
description: Upload a video to a lesson — from the browser straight to secure storage, through processing, to publishing in the lesson
headings: Open the lesson in edit mode
text: Your videos are stored and served through Bunny Stream — secure storage with a built-in player, DRM protection, and download blocking. The upload goes from your browser straight to storage, with no stops in between. This guide covers the whole journey: from an empty lesson to a published video. 1 Open the lesson in edit mode Enter the lesson and switch to Edit mode . A video lesson that doesn't have a video yet shows the message "No video set for this lesson" with the options for adding one. A video lesson with no video — the add options in edit mode 2 Choose the video source There are two ways to add a video to a lesson: Upload a file from your computer — the file goes from your browser straight to WHITEBOARD storage. Paste a URL — paste a video link into the URL field and click Add . Pro tip Don't have a video yet? You can record the lesson right inside the system, teleprompter and editing included — see Getting to know the recording studio . 3 Track the upload While uploading, a progress screen shows the upload percentage, how much of the file size has been uploaded so far, the upload speed, and the estimated time remaining. The system also shows your network connection stability. You can click Pause upload and pick up later, or Cancel upload — canceling stops the process and you'll need to start over. The upload progress screen — percentage, speed, and estimated time Heads-up Don't close the browser window in the middle of an active upload. If your connection is shaky, use Pause upload and continue once the network settles. 4 Wait for processing Once the upload finishes, Bunny Stream processes the video: converting it to a streaming format (HLS), generating a thumbnail, and running a quality check. Processing can take a few minutes, and you can follow the stages on screen. 5 Publish to the lesson When processing finishes, you get a preview of the video with two options: Publish to lesson — the video is placed in the lesson as is. Open in editor — head to the built-in video editor for trims, a logo, an intro, and captions before publishing. Upload complete — publish to the lesson or open in the editor How your video is protected Every video uploaded to the system is served through WHITEBOARD's built-in player, with DRM protection and download blocking — students watch inside the course and can't download the source file. There's nothing to set up: the protection applies automatically to every video that lands in storage. FAQ The upload failed — now what? In most cases it's a network issue. Check your internet connection and click Try again on the error screen — the upload will start over. Can I replace the video in an existing lesson? Yes — open the lesson in edit mode and add a new video in place of the current one. What's next Videos and files you've uploaded are managed in one place — continue to The content library — managing files and videos . And if you feel like polishing the video before publishing, see The built-in video editor .

title: The content library — manage files and videos
description: My library — the one place where every video and file you've uploaded lives, ready to reuse
text: Every video and file you upload to WHITEBOARD is saved in your content library, so you can use it again without re-uploading — in the same course or a different one. Here's how to find your way around. 1 Open the library In the side menu, click My library . My Library in the side menu 2 Find your content The library gathers all the videos and files you've uploaded to the system — including recordings from the recording studio and files you attached to lessons. 3 Use content in your lessons Content from the library can be placed into lessons: a video as the lesson video, and files as attached files or content blocks. The big win is reuse — an intro video, a template deck, or a workbook that serves several courses gets uploaded exactly once, and any future update happens in one place. Good to know Videos in the library are stored and served through Bunny Stream — secure storage with a built-in player, DRM, and download blocking. Details in Uploading videos to WHITEBOARD storage . What's next Once your content is in place, it's worth going over your course settings — pricing, cover image, and viewing settings. And if you haven't uploaded your first video yet, start with Uploading videos to WHITEBOARD storage .

title: Course settings
description: The course settings tab — name, description, URL, cover image, pricing, viewing settings, and deletion
text: The Settings tab on the course page gathers everything that defines your course to the outside world: what it's called, what it costs, how it looks in search, and what students are allowed to do. Changes are saved with the save button in the top bar — as long as you have unsaved changes, the button will show it. 1 The basics At the top, edit the course name and the short description — these appear on the course page and in search. This is also where you'll find the course status (Draft or Published) and the course URL — the unique address where students reach your course. The basic details in the settings tab — name, description, status, and URL Heads-up Once a course is published it can't go back to draft, and the URL locks. Settle on a final URL before publishing. 2 Cover image Upload a main image to display on the course page and in search results. The design recommends a 16:9 ratio at 1280×720 pixels. 3 Pricing and purchase Choose between Free — any student can access at no charge — and Paid , where students purchase access and you set a price in shekels. You can change the pricing at any time. Pricing and purchase — choosing between a free and a paid course 4 Additional settings Toggles that shape the student experience: Completion certificate — students who finish the course automatically receive a certificate. Show student count — the number of enrolled students appears on the public course page. Allow content downloads — students can download attached files for offline viewing. Prerequisites — tags that explain what students should know or prepare before starting. 5 Viewing time limit If you want to limit course access to a fixed window from the moment of purchase, turn on Enable time limit and set a number of days. When the period ends, access locks automatically. Deleting the course The deletion area is at the bottom of the page. Heads-up Deleting a course is irreversible — all data, students, and content are permanently removed. What's next The next step in designing your course is the course brand kit — your own colors, fonts, and logo.

title: Brand kit for a course
description: Customize your course's look — logo, colors, fonts, button shape, and cover image, with a live preview
headings: Upload a logo and cover image
text: The brand kit controls how your course looks to students — your colors, fonts, and logo instead of the system defaults. Every change updates instantly in the preview next to the editor, so you see exactly what your students will get. 1 Open the brand kit On the course page, switch to the Brand kit tab. 2 Upload a logo and cover image In the Course logo card, upload a PNG, SVG, or JPG file. In the Background / cover image card, upload your course's cover image. 3 Set colors and typography In the Colors card, pick a primary color, a secondary color, and a background color — with the color picker or by typing a HEX value. In the Typography card, choose a heading font, a body font, and a text size. The brand kit editor — logo, colors, and typography 4 Choose a button shape In the Buttons card, choose between rounded, semi-rounded, and square. Button color is derived from the primary color you set. 5 Check the preview and save The Preview panel shows the course page with your new kit, updating live. Happy with it? Click Save changes . Changed your mind? Reset to default brings back the system design. A live preview of the brand kit on the course page Pro tip Students see your kit inside the course player too — make sure the colors you picked keep the text readable against the background. What's next Course designed and ready? Time for Publishing and sharing your course .

title: Publish and share your course
description: From draft to live course — publishing at the course level, publishing individual lessons, and sharing the URL with students
text: Publishing in WHITEBOARD works on two levels: the course itself, and each lesson inside it. That means you can publish a live course and keep adding lessons gradually — each lesson goes live only when you decide. 1 Publish the course In the course's Settings tab, under Course status , switch the status from Draft to Published . A published course is visible to students and open for enrollment. The course status in the settings tab — moving from draft to published Heads-up After publishing, the course can't go back to draft, and its URL locks. Make sure the URL is final before you publish. 2 Publish lessons Each lesson is managed separately: a new lesson is born as a Draft and marked that way in the sidebar. To publish it, open the lesson in edit mode and click Publish lesson in the top editing bar. A draft lesson shows students the message "This lesson isn't available yet — coming soon", so you can build the entire structure in advance and reveal it lesson by lesson. The Publish lesson button in the lesson's edit bar 3 Share the course The course's unique URL is set in the Settings tab, under Course URL — that's the address you send to students or embed in your sales page. The course URL for sharing with students Good to know The course page has a Preview button — that's how you check what the course looks like to students, before and after publishing. What the student sees In a published course, students see only the lessons you've published. A lesson still in draft shows the message "This lesson isn't available yet — coming soon" in place of the video, so students know more content is on the way. A draft lesson from the student's perspective — the lesson isn't available yet What's next Your course is live — now invite students to it. See Inviting students to your course .

title: Get to know the recording studio
description: What's inside the WHITEBOARD recording studio and how the flow works — from the lobby to a published lesson
text: The recording studio lets you record entire lessons right in your browser — camera, screen, teleprompter, editing, and captions — no external software, no shuffling files between tools. The result goes straight into a lesson in your course, stored on WHITEBOARD's secure storage and served to students through the built-in player. How the flow works Every recording moves through the same stations: The lobby — name the lesson, upload assets to present (slides and files), set up your camera, mic, and quality, and prep a script for the teleprompter. Active recording — record in takes, switch between camera, screen, and screen + camera modes, and present assets as you go. Takes review — watch every take, delete what didn't work, and choose how to continue. The video editor — cuts, logo, intro and outro, transitions, titles, and captions. Upload and publish — the video uploads to WHITEBOARD storage, gets processed, and lands in the lesson. The recording lobby — lesson details, assets, and a camera preview Where you enter from You reach the recording lobby from inside the course — pick a chapter and record a new lesson into it. Pro tip You don't have to pass through every station: after reviewing your takes you can choose Publish as is and skip editing entirely — or open the editor just for automatic captions. What's next Start recording — Recording a lesson — from the lobby to the final take . Once the recording is ready, move on to Reviewing takes and picking the best version and from there to The built-in video editor .

title: Record a lesson — from the lobby to the final take
description: Setting up your camera and mic in the lobby, recording in takes, and switching between camera, screen, and screen + camera modes
headings: Set up your camera, mic, and quality
text: Recording a lesson in the studio splits into two parts: prep in the lobby, then the recording itself. Good prep in the lobby is what makes the recording easy — once everything's set, all that's left is to hit record and talk. 1 Fill in the lesson details The lobby shows the course and chapter you're recording into, plus a Lesson name field. Under Lesson assets , upload the files you'll want to present during the recording — HTML slides, PPTX, PDF, and images. HTML files render interactively, so you can scroll and interact with them while you record. 2 Set up your camera, mic, and quality Next to the preview, turn on your camera, microphone, and screen share, and pick your devices from the dropdowns. Under Recording settings , choose the shape of the camera window in screen-share mode (rectangle or circle), its size, and its default position on screen, and pick a recording quality. Recording settings in the lobby — camera, mic, window shape, and quality 3 Start recording Click Start recording . You'll get a countdown, and then the recording is off — with a time counter and a REC indicator on screen. The Start recording button in the lobby Pro tip Hitting the spacebar pauses and resumes the recording — handy when you need a moment to breathe or glance at your material. 4 Switch between view modes While recording, you can switch modes at any moment: Camera , Screen + camera , or Screen . The Assets button opens the list of files you uploaded in the lobby — click Show to present an asset, or paste a website link to show it live. The mode switcher in recording — camera, screen + camera, screen 5 Record in takes The center button starts and stops a take. Didn't come out right? Delete the last take and record again — every take is saved so you can choose between them in the review stage. When you're done, click Finish recording and confirm Finish and save . The recording control bar — central record button, delete take, and finish Heads-up Deleting a take during recording requires confirmation and can't be undone. What's next Done recording? Head to Reviewing takes and picking the best version . And if you're working from a script — Working with the teleprompter .

title: Working with the teleprompter
description: Writing a script, tuning speed and size, pause points with ---, and displaying on screen or on an external monitor
text: The teleprompter shows your script on screen while you record, auto-scrolling at a pace you set. That's how you record a polished lesson without memorizing anything — and your eyes stay close to the camera. 1 Write your script Enter your script in the recording lobby, in the teleprompter window — or during the recording via the Teleprompter button, which opens the settings panel. Below the script you'll see the word count and an estimated reading time. Pro tip Add --- between paragraphs to create pause points in the script — a handy way to split the lesson into segments and stop between them. 2 Tune the display The teleprompter panel controls everything about comfortable reading: Scroll speed and navigation buttons between pause points. Font size , text color (white, yellow, or green), and background opacity . Line spacing — compact, normal, or spacious. Focus line — the line marking your current position: top third, center, or bottom third. Mirror — flips the text for working with teleprompter glass. The teleprompter settings panel — script, speed, font, and display 3 Choose where the teleprompter appears Two display modes: On screen — the teleprompter floats above the recording area. Drag it anywhere and resize it as needed. External monitor — the teleprompter opens in a separate window for a second screen, with its own control bar: play, speed, font size, and mirror. The teleprompter floating over the recording screen — focus line and auto-scroll Good to know The teleprompter isn't recorded — it's a helper layer only you can see. Students will see just the video. What's next Record with your script in hand — Recording a lesson — from the lobby to the final take .

title: Review your takes and pick the best version
description: Watching takes on the timeline, deleting what didn't work, and choosing between quick publish and opening the editor
text: Once you finish recording, you land on the takes review screen: this is where you watch everything you recorded, clean out what didn't work, and decide how to continue — quick publish or editing. 1 Watch your takes The player in the center of the screen plays your recording, and below it sits the takes timeline — each take appears as a colored segment, so it's easy to jump between takes and compare. On the side you'll find the takes list with a summary: total duration and number of takes. The takes list on the review screen — total duration and take count 2 Delete what didn't work From the takes list, delete a take that didn't come out well, or choose to re-record it. Heads-up Deleting a take is permanent and can't be recovered. Re-record also overwrites the existing recording with no backup — the system will ask you to confirm before both actions. 3 Complete details and files At the bottom of the screen is the lesson name field, and an Attached files card lets you drag in supporting files to attach to the lesson. 4 Choose how to continue Two ways forward: Open in editor — head to the video editor for cuts, logo, intro, transitions, and captions. Publish as is — the video publishes exactly as recorded. The system will remind you what you're giving up: cuts, brand logo, intro and outro, and captions. The action bar in take review — publish as-is or open in the editor Pro tip Recording a lesson series? Save an editing preset in the editor (logo + intro + captions) and suddenly "Publish as is" isn't so tempting — editing takes minutes. What's next Chose to edit? Continue to The built-in video editor .

title: The built-in video editor
description: Cuts, automatic silence trimming, logo, intro and outro, transitions, titles, and presets — editing without leaving the platform
headings: Brand it: logo, intro, and outro
text: WHITEBOARD's video editor gives you the editing tools a recorded lesson actually needs — no external editing software. The screen has three parts: a preview, a tabbed tools panel, and a timeline with video, audio, and captions tracks. Every change saves automatically. 1 Get to know the tabs The tools panel is split into tabs: Trim , Logo , Intro / outro , Transitions , Captions , Titles , and Preset . The tool tabs in the video editor — trim, logo, intro, transitions, and more 2 Make your cuts In the Trim tab, split the video at any point and cut out unwanted segments, with keyboard shortcuts for the common actions. The smart Trim silent moments tool scans the video and finds silences based on a decibel threshold and minimum duration you set — then cuts them all in one click. Especially useful for those regrouping moments between takes. 3 Brand it: logo, intro, and outro Logo — upload a logo, set its position on a grid, size, and opacity. Intro / outro — choose a template (including an automatic preset built from the course cover image with the chapter and lesson titles), turn on fade-in and fade-out, set a duration — or upload your own clip. The outro also has a CTA template with a call to action. 4 Add transitions and titles In the Transitions tab, drag a transition type (Fade, Dissolve, Slide, Zoom) into the gap between segments on the timeline, and set a duration for each. In the Titles tab, pick a style, type your text, drag the title to where you want it in the preview, and set when and for how long it appears. The timeline in the video editor — video, audio, and caption tracks with transition points 5 Save a preset In the Preset tab, save all your editing settings — logo, intro, outro, transitions, and captions — as a reusable preset, and you can set one to apply automatically to every new video. That's how you keep a consistent look across all your course lessons without setting things up from scratch every time. 6 Export and publish Click Export and publish . Some operations — transitions and animated titles — are processed on the server, so the export may take a few minutes. The progress screen shows each processing stage. What's next Before exporting, it's worth adding captions — Automatic captions and editing them .

title: Automatic captions and how to edit them
description: Generating captions automatically from the audio, fast editing with keyboard shortcuts, styling, burn-in, and SRT export
text: Captions make your lesson accessible — for anyone watching with the sound off, for students who are hard of hearing, and for anyone whose Hebrew is still a work in progress. WHITEBOARD's captions editor generates them automatically from the audio, and all you do is go through and polish. 1 Generate captions automatically Open the captions editor from the Captions tab in the video editor and click Auto-generate . The audio is sent to AI transcription and comes back as a list of captions synced to timestamps. Already have a captions file? Click Import SRT instead. Auto-generating captions in the caption editor 2 Go through and fix The captions appear in a list next to the player — click a caption to jump to its moment in the video, then fix the text and timing. Keyboard shortcuts keep things moving: Enter saves and moves to the next caption, Tab goes to the next, Shift+Tab to the previous. For working on several captions at once, there are bulk actions: delete, merge, and time-shift. 3 Style them In the Caption styling section, set the font size, position (top or bottom), and background — transparent, semi-transparent, or solid. 4 Decide on burn-in The Burn captions into video toggle controls how the captions are delivered: No burn-in — captions display as a separate layer in the player. Styling depends on the viewing player. With burn-in — captions are baked into the video itself, exactly in the style you set. The burn-captions-into-video toggle in the caption editor Good to know Burn-in happens as part of export processing — once burned in, captions can't be turned off in the player. 5 Save and export Click Save . You can also export the captions as an SRT file for use outside the platform. What's next Captions are done — head back to The built-in video editor to export and publish the lesson.

title: What is BOARDi and where you'll find it
description: Meet BOARDi — WHITEBOARD's smart assistant, its task hub, and the ways to start a conversation
headings: Open BOARDi from the main menu
Or just tell BOARDi in your own words
Pick up where you left off
text: BOARDi is WHITEBOARD's smart assistant. It's not a generic chatbot — it's a collection of focused task assistants that sit on top of your data in the platform: a course builder, a student analyst, a sales analyst, and more. In this guide you'll get to know BOARDi's task hub and learn how to reach each assistant from it. 1 Open BOARDi from the main menu In the sidebar, under "Main navigation", click BOARDi . The task hub opens — BOARDi's home screen. BOARDi's Task Hub — greeting, the question field, and the task cards 2 Pick a way to start BOARDi greets you with four task cards: Overview — a status report on the past week, with comparisons across periods and metrics. Data — a deep dive into student, marketing, and sales data. Course builder — build a course from scratch or update an existing one. Retention & email campaigns — emails that win students back and keep them engaged: sequences and campaigns. Clicking a card opens the next level: for example, "Data" splits into student data, marketing data, and sales data, and "Course builder" asks whether to create a new course or update an existing one. Good to know Some cards carry a Coming soon tag — those capabilities are still in development. Cards tagged Ready are available to use. 3 Or just tell BOARDi in your own words You don't have to navigate the cards. In the text field above them, type what you want to do — "Build me a course about photography", "Who's at risk of dropping out?" — and BOARDi picks up on your intent and takes you to the right assistant. 4 Pick up where you left off At the bottom of the task hub there's a Pick up where you left off area — course drafts, overviews, and analyses you've started. Click a row and you're right back to work. The 'Pick up where you left off' area in BOARDi's Task Hub Good to know BOARDi for course creation is available on the Educator plan and up. Full details in the WHITEBOARD plans guide. What's next Ready to build? Head to Building a course with BOARDi's course builder . Want insights about your students? There's the student analyst .

title: Build a course with BOARDi's course builder
description: How BOARDi turns a short conversation into a full course structure — chapters, lessons, and a cover image — and builds it right in the platform
headings: Get the proposal: a cover and a full layout
Build the course in the platform
text: BOARDi's course builder turns a short conversation into a full course structure: chapters, lessons, and a cover image in your brand kit. You answer a few questions, BOARDi drafts a proposal — and once you approve, it sets up the course right in the platform. 1 Open the course builder In BOARDi's task hub, click Course builder and choose: Create new course (start from a blank page) or Update existing course (pick a course and keep developing it). From there, choose where to start — for example Layout builder , which builds the course structure. 2 Answer BOARDi's discovery questions BOARDi asks short questions, one at a time: what the course is about, who it's for, what a graduate should walk away with, how much content you have in mind, and which learning style fits. Most questions you answer by clicking one of the options, and you can always type a free-form answer — or write "you decide" and let BOARDi call it. BOARDi's Course Builder — the chat and the understanding-level meter side by side 3 Watch the course understanding meter On the side of the screen there's a Course understanding meter. The better BOARDi understands your course and its goals, the higher the percentage climbs — and you can see exactly which details it's already nailed down: course subject, target audience, graduate outcome, scope and content, and learning style. The course builder won't build a layout until its understanding is high enough. The 'course understanding level' meter — what BOARDi understands so far 4 Get the proposal: a cover and a full layout Once BOARDi reaches full understanding, it produces two things: an on-brand cover image (with options for Another version , Edit prompt , or Download ) and a complete layout proposal — chapters, lessons, and names, including a summary of the chapter and lesson counts. 5 Fix anything that's off If something in the structure isn't quite right, click Fix . An editing window opens where you can rename chapters and lessons, add a lesson to a chapter or a whole new chapter — then click Save fixes . BOARDi updates the proposal. 6 Build the course in the platform When the structure looks right, click Continue building . BOARDi sets up the course in the platform — chapters, lessons, and names — and opens the course settings screen on the layout tab, where you continue filling in content. Pro tip When the build is done, BOARDi offers to hand the course context over to the email assistant and prep a launch email for your audience — one click and the context carries over. What's next The course now exists in the platform — time to fill it with content. Continue to Building your course structure — chapters and lessons and Uploading videos .

title: The student analyst — ask questions about performance
description: Ask BOARDi about your students, marketing, and sales — and pin insights to the DATA Board to build a report
headings: Pick a topic or ask freely
Pin insights to the DATA Board
text: The student analyst is BOARDi's analytics assistant. Ask it questions in plain language about your students and your business, get answers with charts and live data — and pin the insights that matter to the DATA Board to turn them into a polished report. 1 Open the student analyst In BOARDi's task hub, choose Overview or Data → Student data . Both lead to the student analyst's chat screen. 2 Pick a topic or ask freely BOARDi offers four analysis areas as quick cards: Overview , Marketing , Sales , and Service · Quality (completion, satisfaction, and drop-off points). Click a card — or type your own question in the text field, like "Who's at risk of dropping out right now?". The Student Analyst — the quick-analysis cards in the chat 3 Read the answers and charts BOARDi answers with live data cards: key metrics, breakdowns, trends over time, and funnels that show where students drop off. Alongside the data it adds a BOARDi recommendation — what to do with what you're seeing. 4 Pin insights to the DATA Board Next to every data card and recommendation there's a pin button 📌. Clicking it moves the insight to the DATA Board — the panel on the side of the screen. That's also where you'll find the BOARDi recommends pinning area with hot alerts: students at risk, a drop-off point in a specific lesson, changes in cost per lead, and more. Clicking an alert sends BOARDi the matching question. The Student Analyst's DATA Board — pinned insights and suggestions to pin 5 Download a styled report Once you've pinned what matters, click Download styled report at the top of the DATA Board. BOARDi assembles your pinned insights into a polished, branded report, ready to share. Pro tip Spotted a group of inactive students? BOARDi offers to hand the list and context over to the email assistant and prep a targeted win-back campaign — without leaving the conversation. What's next For a focused look at revenue and transactions, continue to Sales analysis with BOARDi . For managing students by hand — the My students screen .

title: Analyze sales with BOARDi
description: BOARDi analyzes your revenue, funnel, refunds, and top courses — straight from the sales data in the platform
headings: Pick an analysis or ask freely
Keep an eye on refunds and failed payments
Pin insights and download a report
text: BOARDi's sales analysis looks at the business side: revenue, transactions, average order value, refunds, and conversion — based on the sales data recorded in the platform. 1 Open the sales analysis In BOARDi's task hub, choose Data → Sales data . The sales analyst chat opens. 2 Pick an analysis or ask freely BOARDi offers four quick cards: Full sales overview — key metrics, trend, funnel, courses, and payment methods. Conversion funnel — visitor → lead → purchase, including drop-off points. Top courses — revenue per course and expansion potential. Refunds & failed payments — revenue at risk and automatic dunning handling. You can also just type, for example "Give me a sales overview for this month". Sales analysis with BOARDi — the quick-analysis cards 3 Read the full picture The full overview covers the core metrics — monthly revenue, number of transactions, average order value (AOV), refund rate, LTV, and purchase conversion — alongside a year-over-year revenue trend, a payment-method breakdown, and the top courses by revenue. Under each analysis, BOARDi adds a BOARDi recommendation with a practical next step. 4 Keep an eye on refunds and failed payments The Refunds & failed payments card shows refund requests and payments declined at checkout, including their handling status. 5 Pin insights and download a report Just like in the student analyst, every insight can be pinned 📌 to the DATA Board , and at the top of the board you'll find alerts worth checking — a record sales day, abandoned carts, an upsell opportunity. When you're done, click Download styled report to get a branded sales report with everything you pinned. The sales analysis DATA Board — pinning insights and downloading a report Pro tip Want to turn an insight into action? BOARDi offers to hand the audience and insights over to the email assistant — say, an abandoned-cart recovery sequence or an upsell offer for buyers. What's next To understand the student side — the student analyst . For payment settings — Payments and payouts .

title: What knowledge hubs are and which type fits you
description: School, club, and training program — what sets the three knowledge hub types apart, and how to pick the right one for your content
headings: Where to find your knowledge hubs
Club — a community built around your content
Training program — a structured path with sequence and locks
text: A single course is a great start, but once you have several, you need a way to package them together. That's what knowledge hubs are for: three different frameworks that wrap your courses, each suited to a different style of teaching and selling. Where to find your knowledge hubs In the side menu, click My knowledge hubs . At the top of the screen you'll see cards for each type — My courses, Schools, Training programs, and Clubs — with a counter for each. Below them is the list of your existing courses and hubs. The knowledge-hub type cards on the My Knowledge Hubs screen School — your course storefront site A school is a public site that showcases all your courses under one brand: a homepage with an intro video, a course store with categories and tags, and info pages — about, FAQ, and contact. You pick a design template, and every course sells separately at its own price. It's the right fit when you have a catalog of standalone courses and each student buys whatever's relevant to them. Club — a community built around your content A club puts the community front and center: a feed where members post and comment, events (Zoom or in person) with sign-ups and recordings, a chat organized into channels, and a leaderboard that rewards activity. Your courses are available to members, and access is sold as a monthly or yearly subscription — or given away for free. It's the right fit when the real value is the ongoing relationship — mentoring, Q&A, and a sense of belonging — and you want recurring subscription revenue. Training program — a structured path with sequence and locks A training program links several courses into one path with a beginning, middle, and end. You can enforce sequential progress — the next course stays locked until the current one is complete, including a minimum completion percentage. Programs support one-on-one meetings with students, a course workbook that accompanies the lessons, and live sessions. It sells as a single product with a defined access period. It's the right fit for structured professional training — when students need to follow the path you've paved, step by step, with personal guidance. So which do you pick? Several standalone courses, each sold separately — school. An active community and recurring subscription revenue — club. A structured training path sold as one product — training program. Good to know You don't have to pick just one. You could sell courses through a school and run a club for graduates at the same time. Each knowledge hub is managed separately from My knowledge hubs. What's next Picked a type? Head to the matching setup guide: Setting up a school , Setting up a club , or Setting up a training program .

title: Set up a school — your course website
description: How to set up a school in WHITEBOARD — details and URL, cover image, design template, visibility, and publishing
headings: Edit the pages in edit mode
text: In this guide you'll set up a school — a branded course site that showcases all your courses to students and the wider public. By the end, you'll have a live site with its own URL, ready to sell. 1 Open My knowledge hubs In the side menu, click My knowledge hubs . The Schools card at the top of the screen shows how many schools you already have and their status. 2 Create a new school Create a new school from the knowledge hubs screen. Once created, you'll land on the school's management screen, with tabs for Layout, Settings, Brand kit, My students, Email campaigns, and Analytics. Good to know How many course sites you can create depends on your plan — up to 5 course sites on the Educator plan, unlimited on the Leader plan. Full details in WHITEBOARD plans . 3 Fill in the school details In the Settings tab, under School details , fill in: School name — up to 80 characters. Description — up to 300 characters. Shown to students on the school page. URL — the unique address where students will find your school, in the format whiteboard.education/schools/... . School details — name, description, and URL 4 Upload a cover image Under Cover image , upload the main image that appears at the top of your school. We recommend 1280×720 pixels, at a 16:9 ratio. 5 Pick a design template Under School template , choose the style your school will have for students. There are several ready-made templates — see the full comparison in School design templates . Pro tip Want full control over colors, fonts, and logo? Set all of those in the Brand kit tab, with a live preview of both the school page and the invitation email. 6 Set visibility Under Visibility , choose who can see the school: Public — open to everyone, or Private — invite only . Setting the school's visibility — public or private 7 Edit the pages in edit mode Open the school itself. As an instructor, you see it in edit mode: a top bar reads "Edit mode — school", and you can drag courses to reorder them and click any card to edit it. The Preview button shows how the site looks to a student, and the student/instructor toggle in the corner switches between the two views. The edit-mode bar at the top of the school 8 Publish When everything's ready, click Publish changes in the editing bar. Your school goes live at the URL you set. Heads-up Deleting a school is irreversible — all the data, courses, and students attached to it are permanently deleted. The button is at the bottom of the Settings tab. What's next Now set up the store: Your school's course store — course cards, tags, and prices — and round out the info pages .

title: School design templates
description: Classic, Minimal, Natural, Premium, and Waves — what each school design template offers and how to choose
text: The template decides how your school looks to students — the page structure, the hero, and how courses are arranged. Your content stays exactly the same; only the packaging changes, so feel free to experiment. Where to pick a template In the school's Settings tab, under School template , click the template you want. The one marked with a checkmark is the active one. Choosing the design template in school settings Classic A direct, no-frills course page: a short hero with instructor details, a category bar for filtering, a grid of course cards with rating and price, and a meet-the-instructor section at the bottom. Great when you want students to reach the courses as fast as possible. Minimal A clean hero with just a title and subtitle, a search field, and a scrollable course strip with categories. Few distractions — the content does the talking. Natural Structurally similar to Minimal — hero, search, and categories — with a softer visual style. Premium A long, landing-page-style sales page: a big headline with a call to action, an explainer video, a stats strip, a featured course highlighted next to the course grid, a "meet the instructor" section, a student testimonial, and a closing call to action. The right pick when your school doubles as your main sales page. The Premium template hero — a large heading and a call to action Waves A wave-styled hero with a scroll button, a course strip with tags and prices, and feature cards at the bottom (recorded lessons, lifetime access, certificate of completion, personal support). A light, colorful vibe. Pro tip Not sure? Switch templates, click Preview in edit mode, and see how it looks to a student — if it's not right, switch again. What's next Picked a template? Move on to editing the content itself: Your school's course store .

title: Your school's course store
description: Editing your school's course store — banner, categories, course cards, tags, and prices — and what students see
headings: Add courses and expand the list
text: The course store is the heart of your school — the page where students discover, compare, and buy. In this guide you'll edit the store in edit mode: banner, categories, course cards, and tags. 1 Open the courses page In the school's top menu, click Our courses . As an instructor, you see the page in edit mode — click any element to open it for editing. At the top of the page is a banner with a sale tag, a main headline, and a search field for students. The course store's hero banner with a search field 2 Organize categories Below the banner sits the category bar, which filters courses by topic. Categories help students find their way once you have more than a few courses. 3 Edit course cards Every course card in the "Our top courses" strip is editable: Title and price — click the text and edit it directly. Tag — click Edit tag and pick a tag like Bestseller, New, or Top rated. Edit / Delete — the instructor action buttons on the card. Note the "automatic" marker next to rating and progress — those numbers are pulled from the system and can't be edited by hand. A course card in the store with the instructor's edit buttons 4 Add courses and expand the list At the end of the strip is an Add course button for bringing another course into the store. The All courses link opens the full course grid, beyond the featured strip. 5 Edit the feature cards At the bottom of the store are four feature cards (for example: lifetime access, certificate of completion, personal support). Click the edit icon on each card to update its title and text — make sure they match what you actually offer. The benefit cards at the bottom of the course store Pro tip Done editing? Click Publish changes in the editing bar so students see the updated version. What students see A student visiting the store gets the banner, search, and categories — without the editing tools. Courses they're already enrolled in are marked with an "Enrolled" tag and show a progress bar with a Continue learning button; courses they haven't bought yet show a price, a rating, and a purchase button. That way the store serves both new buyers and returning students. Store features Top banner with a sale tag and search Categories for filtering courses Marketing tags for cards: Bestseller, New, Top rated Edit price and previous price right on the card Automatic rating and progress data from the system Feature cards at the bottom of the page What's next The store is ready — now build the trust layer: Info pages — about, FAQ, and contact , and double-check your prices in Pricing a course .

title: Info pages — About, FAQ and Contact
description: Your school's three info pages — editing the about page, the FAQ, and the contact form, and what students see
headings: Open a page in edit mode
text: Someone on the fence about buying isn't just looking at your courses — they're reading about you, hunting for answers, and looking for a way to reach out. Your school's three info pages do exactly that, and in this guide you'll edit all three. 1 Open a page in edit mode The three pages live in the school's top menu: About , FAQ , and Contact . As an instructor, you see them in edit mode — click an element to edit it, and when you're done, click Publish changes in the editing bar. 2 Edit the about page The about page has four sections: Meet the instructor — photo, title, role, and a short bio. Stats strip — courses, students, average rating, years of experience, and lessons. What will you learn here? — cards for your main subject areas. What students say — testimonial cards with a quote, name, and role. The meet-the-instructor area on the About page 3 Edit the FAQ The FAQ page is an accordion: each item shows a question, and clicking it opens the answer. Write the things people actually ask you — content access, certificates, payments, refund policy, and whether it suits beginners. At the bottom of the page, a "Didn't find an answer?" box points to the contact page. An open question on the FAQ page 4 Edit the contact page The contact page lists your contact channels — email, chat, and phone with business hours — plus a Send us a message form with fields for full name, email, subject, and message, alongside your stated response times. The contact form on the Contact page Pro tip Set response times you can actually keep. A "we reply within 24 hours" promise that goes unkept hurts trust more than saying nothing at all. What students see Students reach these pages through the same top menu, minus the editing bar: they read your story on the about page, open questions in the accordion, and send a message from the form. These are the pages that close the deal — worth reviewing them in student mode before you publish. What's next Info pages done? Back to the heart of the site — Your school's course store .

title: Set up a club — a community around your content
description: How to set up a club in WHITEBOARD — details and URL, subscription pricing, member permissions, chat mode, and publishing
headings: Take a look at the club home
text: A club is a knowledge hub built around a community: a feed, events, chat, and a leaderboard — alongside your courses. In this guide you'll set up a club from scratch and decide how its community runs. 1 Create a new club In the side menu, click My knowledge hubs and create a new club from the Clubs card. The club management screen has tabs for Layout, Settings, Brand kit, My members, Email campaigns, and Analytics. 2 Fill in the club details In the Settings tab, under Club details , fill in a name (up to 80 characters), a description (up to 300 characters), and a URL in the format whiteboard.education/clubs/... . This is also where you copy the public link to share with potential members. Club details — name, description, and URL Heads-up You can't change the URL once the club is active. Pick one that'll last. 3 Set pricing Under Pricing & subscription , set a monthly subscription price and a yearly subscription price. Want an open club? Flip the Free club toggle — the price resets to zero and the club opens to everyone at no charge. Club pricing — monthly, yearly, or free Pro tip The recommendation shown on screen: price the yearly plan at 10 months — two months free for anyone committing to a year. 4 Set member permissions Under Membership & permissions , decide what members can do, with a toggle for each permission: Post to the feed Post anonymously to the feed Stay anonymous in the member list Invite members View the leaderboard Member permissions in the club 5 Choose a chat mode Under Club chat , choose how the community communicates: Open chat — everyone talks freely, Teacher-led chat — you run the conversation and members reply, or No chat — the chat is hidden entirely. The club's three chat modes 6 Connect events and a calendar Under Event management , pick a video platform — Google Meet, Zoom, or a custom link — and connect a calendar (Google Calendar, Outlook, and more) so event invites are created automatically. 7 Activate the club Under Status & language , switch the club from Draft — not visible to Active — visible to members , and pick a default language. The homepage includes a welcome card with a welcome video, club stats, recent announcements (add one with Add announcement ), and a list of upcoming events. In edit mode, changes save automatically, and Publish changes pushes them live. A welcome card with a video on the club home What's next The club is up — now bring it to life: The club feed , Events and webinars , and The club chat .

title: The club feed
description: Your club's community feed — publishing posts, organizing by topics, pinning and moderation, and what members see
text: The feed is your club's town square — the place where you and your members post, comment, and feel like a community. In this guide you'll publish your first post, organize the feed by topics, and learn to moderate it. 1 Publish a post Open the club feed from the navigation bar. At the top of the feed is a "Share something with the community..." box — write your post, attach an image or video , and click Post . Your posts carry an "Instructor" tag next to your name, so members spot you right away. The Publish post button in the editing bar does the same thing from anywhere on the screen. The post composer in the club feed 2 Organize by topics Alongside the feed is a Topics list with a post counter for each topic — clicking a topic filters the feed. Every post carries a colored topic tag, so even in a big community it's easy to find the conversations that matter. The topic list that filters the club feed 3 Pin and moderate As an instructor, you have full control over the feed: pin an important post to the top (it appears marked "Pinned by you"), remove posts that don't belong, and filter by topics. Feed settings in the editing bar gathers the moderation options. A post pinned to the top of the feed with the instructor tag Pro tip Who gets to post in the first place? That's set in the club settings, under Membership & permissions — including the option for anonymous posts. Details in Setting up a club . What members see A member opening the feed sees the pinned post first, with the topics list beside it for filtering. To the side is their personal profile card — how many posts they've published, how many likes they've received, and how many courses they're enrolled in. On every post they can like, comment, and share — and if the permission is on, post themselves, even anonymously if you've allowed it. Feed features Posts with text, image, or video Topic tags and filtering by topic Pinning a post to the top and removing posts Likes, comments, and sharing Anonymous posts — if enabled in the club permissions An "Instructor" tag that sets your posts apart What's next Feed alive and kicking? Continue to Events and webinars in the club and The club chat .

title: Events and webinars in your club
description: Creating events and meetups in your club — calendar, automatic invites, recordings, and customer-only webinar rooms — and what members see
text: Events are your club's heartbeat: Zoom meetups, in-person workshops, and webinars that keep members coming back. In this guide you'll create an event, connect a calendar, manage recordings, and open a dedicated webinar room. 1 Create a new event On the Events screen, click New event . Events display in three views — Calendar , List , and Recordings — with month-by-month paging. Each event is marked Online or In person , with a date, time, and location, and it also appears as a colored block on its date in the calendar. The club events calendar 2 Connect video and a calendar In the club settings, under Event management , pick a video platform — Google Meet , Zoom , or a custom link — and connect a calendar (Google Calendar, Outlook, and more). Event invites are then created automatically and land in registrants' calendars. 3 Manage recordings The Recordings tab collects recordings of past sessions, and they also appear in the calendar as a "Recording" block. Members who missed a session catch up from there. 4 Open a webinar room A webinar can get its own dedicated room — a closed channel visible only to customers who registered for the webinar, marked with a Customers only tag and a lock in the channel list. That's where the conversation continues after the session: answering questions and sharing materials. Click New webinar room to create one, and Manage rooms to handle permissions and messages. A webinar room header with the customers-only tag What members see Members see upcoming events on the club homepage and along the side of the events screen — with date, time, type (online or in person), and a Register button. After registering, the invite lands in their calendar, and in webinar rooms they're entitled to, they find the follow-up conversation and materials. Upcoming events with the member's register button Reminders Each member controls their own notifications from their personal profile — under Notification preferences there's a dedicated toggle for Event reminders , alongside club updates and new lessons. Notification preferences in the member's personal profile Event features Three views: calendar, list, and recordings Online events (Zoom/Meet) and in-person events Automatic invites via calendar connection One-click registration and reminders per member preferences Webinar rooms closed to customers only A recordings archive for anyone who missed out What's next The conversation doesn't end when the session does — continue to The club chat .

title: The club chat
description: Your club's group chat — chat modes, building channels by courses and topics, moderating messages, and what members see
text: The chat is your club's running conversation — less formal than the feed, more immediate. In this guide you'll choose how the chat runs, build channels, and learn to moderate the conversation. 1 Choose a chat mode In the club settings, under Club chat , choose how the community communicates: Open chat — everyone talks freely, Teacher-led chat — you run the conversation and members reply, or No chat — the chat is hidden entirely. The setting applies automatically. The club's three chat modes 2 Build channels The conversation is split into channels, organized in groups: General channels (general, announcements, Q&A), Courses — one channel per course, and Topics . Click New channel to add one. Good channel structure keeps conversations focused — questions about a specific course don't get mixed up with general chatter. The channel list in the club chat 3 Moderate the conversation The Manage channels button in the editing bar opens the structure management, and inside channels you can remove messages. Your messages carry an Instructor tag (and in webinar rooms — Host ), so your official answers stand out in the conversation. What members see Members see the channel list with an indicator dot on channels that have new messages. Inside a channel: a header with a description and member count, messages grouped by day, and their own messages aligned to the opposite side. At the bottom is a message box with file attachments. Webinar rooms they're not entitled to are marked with a lock — only registered customers get in. A conversation in a club chat channel — the member's view Good to know The club chat lives alongside the feed, not instead of it: the feed is for deeper conversations that stick around, the chat is for the day-to-day flow. If that feels like too much for your community — the "Teacher-led chat" or "No chat" mode cuts down the noise. Chat features Three conversation modes: open, teacher-led, or no chat Channels by courses, topics, and general channels Unread message indicators Instructor and Host tags on your messages Message removal and channel management Webinar rooms locked to customers only What's next Want to reward your most active members? Continue to The leaderboard and member engagement .

title: The leaderboard and member engagement
description: How the club leaderboard works, what earns points, and how to track and manage your members
headings: Decide whether members see the leaderboard
text: The leaderboard turns club activity into a game: members earn points for learning and participating, and watch themselves climb the rankings. In this guide you'll get to know the leaderboard and the members screen that goes with it. 1 Open the leaderboard Open the Leaderboard from the club's navigation bar. At the top of the screen is a podium with the top three members, and below it the full ranking table — member, points, lessons, and change in position. The This week , This month , and All time tabs switch the time range. The leaderboard — the top-three podium and the table 2 Understand what earns points As shown on screen: points are calculated from completed lessons, posts, event participation, and more. In edit mode you can set scoring rules and reset rankings. 3 Decide whether members see the leaderboard A public ranking isn't right for every community. In the club settings, under Membership & permissions , the Members can view the leaderboard toggle decides whether the leaderboard is visible to members or just a tool for you. 4 Track your members The Members screen shows all club members as cards, with search and quick filters: All , Active , Instructors , New . Each card shows the member's activity stats (posts, lessons, points) and a status tag like "Active" or "Very active" — so you can easily spot both your stars and the members who've gone quiet and could use a nudge. The grid of member cards in the club 5 Manage your members Each member card has instructor Edit and Remove buttons, and the Invite members button in the editing bar grows the community. Members can invite others themselves only if you've turned on that permission in the settings. Pro tip The leaderboard is more powerful when you talk about it: shout out the month's top members in a pinned feed post or at a session — it rewards the active ones and reminds everyone that activity counts. What's next Community buzzing? Now dive into its content — The club feed and Events and webinars in the club , or head back to the club settings .

title: Set up a training program
description: How to set up a training program — adding courses to the path, building chapters and lessons, setting details and pricing, and publishing
headings: Set the price and access period
text: A training program packages several courses into one structured path — with a sequence, locks, one-on-one meetings, and a single price.
