Most are active from the moment you start, without you doing a thing; some marketing data needs a one-time, one-click connection — no API keys, no code. In this guide you'll see what's already connected and what's worth connecting. 1 Open the connections screen Go to Settings and choose Connections · Data sources . 2 What's always on Under Built into the platform you'll find the sources that are available from day one: Students and progress Sales and revenue Watch time Email campaigns and CRM Ratings and satisfaction Course content The built-in data sources — always on, no setup required These need zero setup — everything that happens on the platform is already being counted. 3 Check how much of the picture BOARDi sees At the top of the screen is a coverage meter — what percentage of the full picture is available to BOARDi right now. The more sources you connect, the higher the meter climbs and the broader the insights get. 4 Connect external sources Under External connections , connect your marketing data in one click: Meta · Facebook & Instagram — one connection that unlocks ad data, conversions, and organic data from Facebook and Instagram, including the Facebook Pixel. After connecting, you pick a Facebook page, Instagram account, ad account, and Pixel. Google Analytics — traffic, referral sources, and sessions for your course site (GA4). Google Ads — your Google campaign performance, cost, and return. The external connections — Meta, Google Analytics, and Google Ads in a one-time connection Good to know Next to each connection there's a "?" button linking to that connection's full setup guide. 5 And if you don't connect? Nothing breaks. BOARDi shows what it has, and when it's missing a data point it guides you right in the conversation — for example: "To see cost per lead, connect your ad account". Connect only when it's relevant to you. What's next Once your sources are connected, head back to the analytics screen — or ask BOARDi about your sales directly: Sales analysis with BOARDi .

title: Your account's global settings
description: A tour of the Settings screen — payments, email settings, integrations, team & permissions, and the partner program
text: The Settings screen brings together everything that applies to your whole account — not to a specific course: payments, email sending, integrations, team members, and the partner program. In this guide we take a quick tour of every tab. 1 Open Settings In the sidebar, click Settings . There's a save indicator at the top of the screen — when it says "All changes saved," you can leave with peace of mind. The tab bar of the global settings screen 2 Payments At this stage there's no built-in payments connection in the platform — payments connect to your courses through the WHITEBOARD app on Make. The full guide: Payments and getting paid . 3 Email settings This tab controls how your emails look in your recipient's inbox: Domain verification — verify your domain to send from a custom address and improve deliverability. Sender details — sender name, sender email, reply-to email, and a physical address (required by international email standards like CAN-SPAM). Test email — Send test email confirms your settings work before a real audience receives anything. The Email settings tab — domain verification, sender details, and a test email 4 Integrations External connections: Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, Vimeo, Make.com, and Zapier (coming soon). The full breakdown is in Integrations — analytics, Pixel, Vimeo, and more . 5 Team & permissions Add team members with Add team member — each with their own role and permissions. Handy when you have a community manager, a content editor, or a business partner who needs access without sharing your password. 6 Partner program Every account gets a unique partner link. Anyone who signs up for WHITEBOARD through your link earns you a 10% commission for the customer's lifetime, paid out quarterly. The screen shows your active referred customers and your next expected payout — and there's a CSV export here too. What's next The tab with the biggest impact on your revenue is payments — Payments and getting paid .

title: Team & permissions — grant course-management access
description: How to add a team member with their own permissions — a content editor, community manager, or partner — without sharing your password
headings: Choose a role and access scope
text: As the business grows, you stop doing everything yourself: a content editor uploading lessons, a community manager answering in chat, an accountant who needs the finance report. The permissions system lets you bring them into your account — each with their own access, without sharing a password and without them seeing anything that isn't theirs to see. Good to know Permissions apply to your admin area only. Students never see your team members, and a team member doesn't become a student in your courses. 1 Go to Team & permissions In the sidebar, click Settings , then choose Team & permissions in the tab bar. The Team & permissions tab — the team member list 2 Add a team member Click Add team member and enter the email address of the person you're bringing on. They get the invitation by email — and sign in with their own account, not your password. The Add team member button — highlighted with a ring 3 Choose a role and access scope Each team member gets a role and an access scope — say, Course management for someone who builds and updates content, or reports-only access for whoever handles the finances. The scope is shown on the team member's card, so you can always see at a glance who can touch what. A team member card — role, access scope, and actions 4 Manage your team over time From a team member's card you can, at any time: Edit their role and scope — when someone takes on more (or less) responsibility Remove a team member — access is blocked immediately, no password change needed Search the list — handy as the team grows Pro tip Working with an external video editor on a single project? Give them narrow access to managing just that course, and when the project wraps — remove them in one click. That's the beauty of it: exactly the access they need, for exactly as long as they need it. Heads-up The Admin role grants broad access, including settings and finances. Save it for true partners — for everyone else, a focused role is enough.

title: The brand kit — logo, colors and fonts
description: Set your logo, brand colors, and typography — with a live preview of your landing page, emails, and course page
text: Your brand kit controls how everything looks on the outside: your landing page, your emails, and your course page all inherit the logo, colors, and fonts you set here. Set it up once, and your brand stays consistent at every customer touchpoint. 1 Open the brand kit Open your course from My knowledge hubs and select the Brand kit tab. On one side you'll see the editing panel, and on the other a live preview that updates with every change. 2 Upload your logo Drag a file into the upload area or click it. PNG, SVG, and JPG are supported, up to 2MB. To remove a logo, click the remove button next to the current file. 3 Set your brand colors There are five color roles, each with a note on where it shows up: Primary color — buttons, headings, and key elements. Secondary color — highlights, progress bars, and links. Text color — the main text across your pages. Background color — the overall background of your course page. Button color — your CTA buttons, like the enroll button. Below the colors there's a Corner roundness slider that controls how rounded your buttons are, with a live sample button. The brand kit edit panel — logo, brand colors, and corner rounding 4 Choose your fonts In the Text tab, pick a font for each level: main heading (H1), subheading (H2), body text, and quote. A live sample of the text in your chosen font appears below each selection. 5 Check the live preview In the preview bar, switch between the three views your customers see — Landing page , Emails , and Course page — and between desktop and mobile . That way you see your brand in every context before you publish. The live preview of the brand kit — landing page, emails, and course page, desktop and mobile 6 Save Click Save changes . The save indicator at the top tells you if there are unsaved changes. Reset returns the kit to its default values. Pro tip Pick a button color that stands out against your background color — that's the button that sells. The landing page live preview is the place to check it. What's next Your colors and fonts also apply to your emails — see the visual email editor — and to your course landing page .

title: Integrations — an overview
description: The WHITEBOARD integrations map — what each connection gives you and where to go to set it up
text: WHITEBOARD ships with built-in integrations for the tools you already work with — Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, and Vimeo, with Zapier on the way. The screen under Settings → Integrations groups them all together, each with a status: connected, not connected, or coming soon. This article is a quick map — every connection has its own guide with the full setup steps. The Data & marketing group on the integrations screen — Meta and Google Analytics Data & marketing Connecting Meta — Facebook Pixel — one connection to your Meta account that unlocks ad data, Pixel conversions, and organic data from Facebook and Instagram. Connecting Google — Google Analytics — traffic, visit sources, and sessions for your course site (GA4), plus campaign data from Google Ads. These connections also feed BOARDi's insights — see Connections and data sources . Calendar & meetings Connecting Google Calendar — sync meetings to your calendar with automatic Google Meet links in every invite. Automation & CRM Connecting Make — automations — an API key and a webhook that send every event (lead, purchase, cancellation) to your Make.com scenarios. Zapier — connect to thousands of apps. Marked "coming soon." Video Connecting Vimeo — import existing videos from your Vimeo account, as an alternative to the built-in storage. Pro tip No need to connect everything up front. Start with what serves you right now — Meta if you're advertising, Analytics if traffic tracking matters to you — and add the rest as the need comes up. What's next Advertising on Facebook or Instagram? Start with the highest-impact connection — Connecting Meta .

title: Connect Meta — Facebook Pixel
description: Connect your Meta account — ads, Pixel conversions, and organic data from Facebook and Instagram — step by step
headings: Copy the App ID and App Secret
Connect a webhook for Lead Ads (only if you need it)
text: One connection to your Meta account unlocks all your marketing data: impressions, CTR, cost per lead, ROAS, Pixel conversions, and Instagram data — all flowing into your analytics and BOARDi's insights. Setup is one-time, about 6 minutes, without a single line of code: the built-in setup guide generates all the codes for you — you just copy and paste. The full setup guide is also available inside the platform: Settings → Integrations → Meta → "?" → Setup guide . Next to the guide is a Your connection details panel — fill in the fields and the codes are generated automatically. The built-in setup guide for connecting Meta — steps and the connection-details panel 1 Create a Meta app Go to developers.facebook.com → My Apps → Create App → choose the Business type. This is the app BOARDi will read data through — you create it once. 2 Copy the App ID and App Secret In the app dashboard → Settings → Basic . Copy the App ID and App Secret and paste them into the connection details panel in the guide. Heads-up The App Secret is a secret key — don't publish it and don't send it in chat. Paste it only into its dedicated field, where it's stored encrypted. 3 Paste the Redirect URI In Facebook Login → Settings , in the Valid OAuth Redirect URIs field, paste the URL the guide generated for you. It must match exactly — otherwise sign-in will fail. 4 Verify your domain In Business Settings → Brand Safety → Domains , add your domain and choose Meta-tag verification. BOARDi automatically embeds the tag the guide generates into your course site. 5 Connect a webhook for Lead Ads (only if you need it) Running lead campaigns? In Webhooks → Page , paste the Callback URL and Verify Token from the panel — and every new lead is sent in real time. If not — skip this. 6 Choose assets and approve Head back to the connections screen in WHITEBOARD, click Connect on the Meta card, sign in, and choose which assets to expose: Facebook page, Instagram account, ad account, and Pixel. All permissions are read-only . That's it — BOARDi is connected. What you get Once connected, you get: Ad data — impressions, CTR, cost per lead, and ROAS. Pixel conversions on your course site. Organic data — Facebook page engagement and Instagram followers. Leads from campaigns straight in (through the webhook). What's next Check the Connections and data sources screen to confirm the connection is active and BOARDi's coverage meter went up. Advertising on Google too? Continue to Connecting Google — Google Analytics .

title: Connect Google — Google Analytics
description: Connect Google Analytics and Google Ads — traffic, visit sources, and campaign performance inside WHITEBOARD
headings: Paste the Redirect URI and JS Origin
text: The Google connection brings your course site traffic inside — visit sources and sessions from GA4 — and if you run ads, your Google Ads campaign performance too: impressions, cost per lead, and ROAS. Setup is one-time, about 6 minutes, no code: the built-in setup guide generates all the URLs for you — you just copy and paste. The full guide is available inside the platform: Settings → Integrations → Google Analytics → "?" → Setup guide , alongside a Your connection details panel that generates the URLs automatically. The built-in setup guide for connecting Google — Analytics and Ads 1 Create a Google Cloud project Go to console.cloud.google.com → New Project and give it a name (say, "WHITEBOARD"). The project is the container for all your connection settings — you create it once. 2 Enable the APIs In APIs & Services → Library , enable two: Google Analytics Data API (returns traffic, sources, and sessions from GA4) and Google Ads API (returns impressions, cost per lead, and ROAS from your campaigns). 3 Set up the consent screen In OAuth consent screen , choose External , fill in an app name and support email, and add the Analytics and Ads scopes — read-only . 4 Create an OAuth Client ID In Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth client ID , choose the Web application type. Once created, you get a Client ID and Client Secret — paste them into the connection details panel. They're stored encrypted. 5 Paste the Redirect URI and JS Origin On the same OAuth Client screen, paste the Authorized redirect URI and the JavaScript origin the guide generated for you. Both must match exactly. 6 Connect and approve Head back to the connections screen in WHITEBOARD, click Connect on Google Analytics and/or Google Ads, sign in with your Google account, and approve. BOARDi is connected. What you get Course site traffic — visitors, sessions, and visit sources (GA4). Google campaign performance — impressions, clicks, cost per lead, and ROAS. The data feeds BOARDi's insights alongside your sales and enrollments. Good to know You can connect just Analytics without Ads — and add Ads later, when you start advertising. What's next Once connected, Connections and data sources shows the status and your updated coverage meter. Advertising on Meta too? Connecting Meta — Facebook Pixel .

title: Connect Vimeo
description: Create a Vimeo Access Token and connect it to WHITEBOARD to import your existing videos into courses
headings: Create an app in Vimeo Developer
Fill in a name and description
Create an Access Token with the right scopes
Paste the token in WHITEBOARD and save
text: Already have a video library on Vimeo? This connection lets you import those videos straight into your courses — no downloading and re-uploading. It's an optional alternative: your core course video lives on WHITEBOARD's built-in storage. The connection takes one Access Token, in five steps. The full setup guide is available inside the platform: Settings → Integrations → Vimeo → "?" → Setup guide . The built-in setup guide for connecting Vimeo — creating an Access Token 1 Create an app in Vimeo Developer Go to developer.vimeo.com → My Apps → Create App . This is the developer app WHITEBOARD will read your videos through — you create it once and it stays in your account. 2 Fill in a name and description Enter an App name (say, "WHITEBOARD Import") and a short App description , accept the terms, and click Create . The name is for your own reference only — write whatever works for you. 3 Create an Access Token with the right scopes On the app page → Authentication tab → Generate an Access Token section → check exactly three scopes: public , private , and video_files , then click Generate . These permissions are enough to see your videos and pull the video files — with no permission to edit or delete anything. 4 Copy the Access Token The token is shown only once , right after it's created — copy it now. Lost it? Just create a new token. Heads-up The Access Token is a secret key that grants access to your Vimeo account. Don't share it and don't send it in chat — paste it only into its dedicated field, where it's stored encrypted. 5 Paste the token in WHITEBOARD and save Back in WHITEBOARD → Settings → Integrations → Vimeo → paste the Access Token into the field and click Save . The platform verifies the connection — and you can start importing videos. What you get Import existing videos from Vimeo straight into your course lessons. Read-only access — WHITEBOARD never edits or deletes anything in your Vimeo account. What's next New videos you record go straight to the built-in storage — see Uploading videos to WHITEBOARD storage .

title: Connect Google Calendar
description: Sync meetings to Google Calendar with automatic Google Meet links in every invite — a one-click connection
text: Connecting Google Calendar makes every meeting booked in WHITEBOARD — consultation calls, student sessions — land in your calendar automatically, with a Google Meet link ready in the invite. It's the simplest connection of them all: a regular Google sign-in, no keys and no codes. The full setup guide is available inside the platform: Settings → Integrations → Google Calendar → "?" → Setup guide . The built-in setup guide for connecting Google Calendar 1 Click "Connect calendar account" In Settings → Integrations , under Calendar & meetings , click Connect calendar account . Google's official sign-in window opens — WHITEBOARD never sees your password. Choose the Google account your meetings should be written to. 2 Approve the calendar permission In Google's consent window, approve the Calendar permission. It lets WHITEBOARD create, update, and delete meeting events only — not read the rest of your calendar. That's the only permission required. 3 Choose your calendar You're back in WHITEBOARD — now pick the calendar your meetings should be written to from the list and click Save . Pro tip You can route meetings to a dedicated calendar (say, "Meeting schedule") to keep them separate from your personal one. 4 Turn on Google Meet links Flip the Automatically create Google Meet link toggle. From now on, every new meeting gets its own Meet link, embedded in the invite sent to participants — they click and join. 5 Test with a demo meeting Click Create demo meeting — a test event is created in your chosen calendar, complete with a Meet link. Open Google Calendar and confirm the event and link showed up. Once you've checked, you can delete the demo event. What you get Every meeting booked in the platform is written to your chosen calendar automatically. A Google Meet link is created and embedded in every invite. Participants get the invite with the link — no manual coordination. What's next Live meetings are part of training programs — see Program layout — order, locks, and meetings .

title: Connect Make — automations
description: Connect Make.com with an API key and a webhook — every lead, purchase, and cancellation flows to your automations in real time
headings: Create an API key in WHITEBOARD
Map fields and turn it on
text: WHITEBOARD has an official app on Make — with ready-made modules (like add student , which adds a student to a course) and a clear guide for connecting your courses. Through it, you connect the platform to any external process: a purchase at your payment provider that automatically becomes a student in a course, a new lead sent to WhatsApp, a subscription cancellation that triggers an alert. The connection works in both directions — an API key that identifies your account, and a webhook that receives every event in real time. Here's a real scenario built on the app — capturing purchases from the payment provider and routing them as students into the right courses: The full setup guide is available inside the platform: Settings → Integrations → Make.com → "?" → Setup guide . The built-in setup guide for connecting Make.com — API key and Webhook 1 Create an API key in WHITEBOARD In Settings → Integrations , on the Make.com card, click Create API key . A key unique to your account is created and shown on screen. 2 Copy the key Click the copy button next to the key (it starts with wb_ ). The full key is shown only once — save it before you move on. Heads-up Lost the key? Create a new one — but that revokes the old one immediately, and any scenario using it will stop working until you update it. 3 Add a connection in Make.com In Make.com → New Scenario → add a WHITEBOARD module → Add connection → paste your API key into the API Key field and click Save . 4 Copy the webhook URL Copy the scenario's webhook URL from Make (it starts with hook.eu2.make.com ) and paste it into the Webhook URL field on the Make.com card in WHITEBOARD — this is where every new event will be sent: lead, purchase, cancellation. 5 Map fields and turn it on In Make, map the fields coming from WHITEBOARD (name, email, product, amount) to the actions you want — a WhatsApp message, a row in Google Sheets, whatever you build — and click ON . Test with Run once and a demo event. What you get Payments connection — the app is how you connect your payment provider to your courses: a purchase webhook comes in, an add student module adds the customer to the course. The full guide: Payments and getting paid . Real-time events: new leads, purchases, and subscription cancellations. One API key for all the courses and clubs in your account. Cancellation alerts — the integrations screen has a Subscription cancellation reminders toggle that sends an alert through the webhook when a subscription is canceled or about to end, to the recipients you set. Send test — sends a demo message to the webhook to confirm the pipeline works. The Automation & CRM group on the integrations screen — Make.com, cancellation reminders, and Zapier What's next The events sent to Make are born in the CRM — worth getting to know CRM — all your contacts in one place . And if you're waiting on Zapier — it's marked "coming soon" in the integrations overview .

title: Log in and enter your first course
description: How to sign in to WHITEBOARD for the first time and get to the course you enrolled in
text: Got access to a course on WHITEBOARD? Great. You'll be inside in under a minute. Here's how to sign in for the first time and go straight to your lesson. 1 Open the invitation Your instructor sends you an invitation or a link to the course. Click the link — it takes you to the platform's sign-in screen. 2 Sign in Enter your details and sign in. If it's your first time, you may be asked to fill in a few basics like your name and a photo. 3 Land on My courses After signing in, you land on the My courses screen — your home base in the platform. This is where all the courses you have access to appear, along with your progress in each one. The student's My Courses screen 4 Enter your first course Find your course and click Start learning (or Continue learning if you've already begun). The course player opens on the first lesson — and from here, you just learn. Pro tip Next time you won't need the invitation link — just go to the site and sign in, and your courses will be waiting right where you left them. What's next Worth getting to know the rest of the screens — Finding your way around — My courses and My library .

title: Finding your way around — My Courses and My Library
description: A quick tour of the platform — the side menu, the My courses screen, and what's waiting for you in each area
headings: Get to know the side menu
text: A few minutes of looking around and you'll feel right at home. In this guide we'll walk through the side menu, the My courses screen, and the other areas you'll use day to day. 1 Get to know the side menu The side menu follows you throughout the platform. Here's what it holds in student mode: My courses — all your courses, with your progress in each one. My clubs — the communities you're a member of. My summaries — all the notes you've written while learning. Settings — your profile and preferences. At the bottom of the menu you'll find the View mode toggle (student / instructor) — only relevant if you also teach on the platform — and your profile. The side menu in student mode 2 The My courses screen This is your home screen, and it has three areas: Stats row — how many active courses you have, how many you've completed, and your average progress. Pick up where you left off — the courses you watched most recently; one click takes you back to the lesson. My learning — all your courses as cards, with the instructor's name, lesson count, and a progress bar. The student's My Courses screen Pro tip You can filter your courses (All / In progress / New / Completed), sort, and search — handy once you're enrolled in more than a course or two. 3 My library The library gathers your content into folders — for example a My courses folder and a Content folder with files. You can search, switch between grid and list views, and click a folder to browse inside. The library — content folders 4 Small buttons worth knowing In the top bar of every screen you'll find: Theme toggle — switch between light and dark mode. Language toggle — Hebrew / English. What's next Now that you know your way around — here's what Watching lessons and tracking progress looks like.

title: Reset your password and login details
description: Forgot your password or want to update your login details? Here's how to do it in a minute
headings: Open the email and choose a new password
text: Forgot your password? Happens to everyone. The reset takes a minute, and you can do it yourself — no need to wait for your instructor. 1 Click "Forgot password" On the sign-in screen, below the password field, click the Forgot password link. 2 Enter your email Type the email address you enrolled in the course with — the same address your instructor sent the invitation to. A reset link will be sent to that email. Pro tip Not sure which email it was? Search your inbox for the original course invitation — the address that received it is the right one. 3 Open the email and choose a new password Click the link in the email, choose a new password, and confirm. From that moment on, you sign in with the new password. Didn't get the email? Check your spam / promotions folder. Make sure you typed exactly the address you enrolled with. Still nothing — reach out to your course instructor; they can check which address you're registered under. Updating personal details Your name, photo, and other details are updated in your personal profile inside the platform.

title: Quick access — keep your course always within reach
description: Saving a shortcut to your course on your phone and computer, staying signed in, and what to do when your internet is shaky
headings: Add a shortcut to your phone's home screen
text: Your course works in any browser, on any device. A few small steps will save you from hunting for the link every single time. 1 Save the right link The address you use is the link you got from your instructor (or the address of their school / club). Bookmark it in your browser — and you'll be in your lesson with one click. 2 Add a shortcut to your phone's home screen iPhone (Safari): open the course → the share button → Add to Home Screen . Android (Chrome): open the course → the three-dot menu → Add to Home screen . From now on, the course opens from your phone just like an app. 3 Stay signed in Sign in once from your personal device — and the platform remembers you next time. If you're on a public or shared computer, it's better to sign out when you're done. Tips for smooth watching Your progress is saved automatically — you can stop mid-lesson and pick up from the same spot on another device. Slow internet? Try lowering the video quality in the player. What's next Signed in and set up? Now's a good time to meet the learning tools — My notes and Chatting with BOARDi .

title: Watch lessons and track your progress
description: Inside the course player — moving between chapters and lessons, attached files, playback speed, and marking a lesson complete
headings: Get your bearings in the player
text: Most of your time in a course will be spent in the player — the screen where you watch lessons. In this guide we'll get to know it: how to move between lessons, where the attached files live, and how the platform tracks your progress. 1 Get your bearings in the player The screen is split into three parts: Sidebar — the course structure: chapters, lessons, and your progress bar. Lesson area — the video or content of the current lesson, with attached files below it. Thin side rail — quick buttons for the course notebook, notes, BOARDi, and settings. The course player — an overview in student mode 2 Move between chapters and lessons In the sidebar, each chapter opens and closes with a click, and every lesson shows its name and length. Lessons you've finished are marked, and the current lesson is highlighted. There's also a Search lesson... field for finding a specific one. The course sidebar — chapters, lessons, and progress A course can also include lesson types that aren't video — like a quiz, a downloadable file, or an embedded interactive tool. 3 Watch at your own pace In the bottom bar: Previous / Next — move between lessons. Playback speed — from 0.5× up to 2×. Your place in the course — "Lesson X of Y". The bottom bar in the player — navigation, speed, and mark-as-complete Pro tip In the player settings there's an Autoplay next lesson toggle — when it's on, the next lesson starts on its own. 4 Download attached files Below the lesson there's an Attached files area — slides, practice sheets, and anything else the instructor added. Click Download next to the file you want. 5 Mark your progress When you finish a lesson, click Mark as complete in the bottom bar. The progress bar in the sidebar updates ("2 / 5 lessons"), and your progress is saved on the My courses screen too. 6 Answer in the course notebook In some lessons the instructor adds questions — open-ended, multiple choice, true/false, or a file upload. They're gathered in the course notebook on the side rail, and your answers are saved there by chapter. What's next While you watch, it's worth jotting things down for yourself — here's how My notes — time-stamped notes work.

title: My notes — timestamped notes
description: Writing notes while you watch, jumping back to the exact moment in the video, and exporting a notebook to PDF
headings: Write a note during a lesson
View a tidy notebook and export to PDF
text: A note written at the right moment is worth gold when you review the material. On WHITEBOARD, every note you write during a lesson is tied to that point in the video — click it later and you jump straight to the moment you wrote it. 1 Write a note during a lesson In the course player, click the notes button on the side rail. The My notes panel opens — write your note and click Save note . The note is saved together with the video's current timestamp. The My Notes panel inside the course player 2 Open My summaries All your notes from all your courses are gathered on the My summaries screen (in the side menu). Each note appears as a card with the course name, the lesson, a content preview — and a timestamp . My Summaries screen — note cards with timestamps 3 Jump to the right moment Clicking the timestamp on a note (say, 14:32) opens the lesson and jumps the video to that exact point. No need to remember "where did they say that" — the note remembers for you. Pro tip Write a quick note whenever the instructor says something worth coming back to. Even two words are enough — the timestamp does the rest. 4 Filter and search At the top of the screen you can filter ( All / By course ), search inside your notes, and sort by date or course. 5 View a tidy notebook and export to PDF In the By course view, your notes arrange themselves like a notebook — by chapters and lessons, with timestamps next to each summary. From there you can click Export notebook to PDF and get a clean file of all your summaries in the course, with the option to include chapter headings and timestamps. A notebook view by course with PDF export What's next BOARDi can write summaries straight into your notes too — see Chatting with BOARDi inside the course .

title: The course workbook — in training programs
description: A digital workbook that accompanies your training program — questions and practice alongside the lessons, with answers saved automatically
headings: What's the difference between the workbook and notes?
text: In training programs, alongside the lessons, you'll find the course workbook — a digital workbook your instructor built for you: questions, exercises, and assignments that move with you through the program. 1 Open the workbook You open the workbook from inside the training program. Each chapter in the workbook is tied to a lesson or topic in the program, so the practice arrives right after the relevant material. 2 Answer at your own pace Type your answer right into the workbook. Answers are saved automatically — you can leave mid-way, come back tomorrow, and continue exactly where you stopped. 3 Track your progress The workbook's progress bar shows how much you've completed. A full workbook is a great way to make sure you're ready for the final exam. Pro tip The workbook isn't an exam — there's no grade and no "forbidden" mistakes. It's the place to think in writing, experiment, and revisit your answers before the real exam. What's the difference between the workbook and notes? The course workbook — questions your instructor wrote, in a fixed structure that follows the program. My notes — your own free-form notes, on any moment in any lesson. The full guide . What's next Finished the workbook? You're probably ready — Taking an exam and getting results .

title: The feed — your community in the club
description: Entering the club, reading and posting in the feed, filtering by topics, and updating your profile
text: The feed is the heart of the club — it's where your instructor posts updates, members share experiences and questions, and you can join the conversation. Here's how to get in and find your way around. 1 Enter the club In the side menu, click My clubs . Every club you're a member of appears as a card with the member count, the number of courses, and your progress through the content. Click Enter club . My Clubs screen — the club cards 2 Read the feed The posts run down the center of the feed: from your instructor (marked with an Instructor tag) and from community members. Important posts the instructor pinned appear first with a pin marker. Under every post — like, comments, and share. The club feed — a compose box and posts 3 Filter by topics The side column shows a list of Topics (like "Q&A") with the post count for each. Click a topic to filter the feed — read only what interests you. 4 Publish a post In the "Share something with the community..." box at the top of the feed, write your post, attach a photo or video if you'd like, and click Publish . Pro tip The side column also has your activity card — how many posts you've published, how many likes you've received, and which courses you're in. 5 Update your profile From the club's side navigation rail, go to My profile : a photo, personal details, and a few words about yourself — and below that, Notification preferences (club updates, new lessons, event reminders). When you're done, click Save changes . My profile in the club — details and notification preferences What's next Beyond the feed, there are also Events and meetups in the club and The club chat waiting for you.

title: Events and meetups in the club
description: The club's event calendar — Zoom meetups, in-person workshops, registration, and recordings of past sessions
text: A good club doesn't happen only on screen — there are Zoom meetups, in-person workshops, and Q&A sessions. In the events area you see everything on one calendar, register with a click, and catch up on recordings of anything you missed. 1 Open the events area In the club's side navigation rail, click the events icon. At the top of the screen there are three tabs: Calendar , List , and Recordings . 2 Look at the calendar In the Calendar view, every event is marked on its day, color-coded by type: online meetup, in-person meetup, or recording. Move between months with the navigation arrows. The club's events calendar 3 Register for an event On the side of the screen you'll see Upcoming events — each one with its date, time, location (Zoom or a physical address), and an Online / In person tag. Click Register to save your spot. Upcoming events — event details and the register button Pro tip Turning on Event reminders in the notification preferences of your profile will make sure you never miss a meetup. 4 Watch recordings of past meetups Missed a session? The Recordings tab gathers the recordings of meetups that already happened — jump in and watch whenever it suits you. What's next Between meetups, the conversation keeps going in the club chat .

title: The club chat
description: The club's chat channels — how to move between channels, send messages, and never miss a thing
text: The chat is where the club's everyday conversation happens — less formal than the feed, faster than email. It's organized into channels by topic, just like any chat app you know. 1 Open the chat In the club's side navigation rail, click the chat icon. The screen splits in two: the channel list on the side, and the conversation in the center. 2 Pick a channel Channels are arranged in groups — for example General channels (general, announcements, Q&A), channels by course , and channels by topic . A channel with messages you haven't read shows a small counter. Click a channel to open its conversation. The list of club chat channels 3 Read and join in At the top of the conversation you'll see the channel's name and description. Messages are grouped by day, and messages from the instructor carry an Instructor tag. Type in the message bar at the bottom and hit send — you can attach files too. A conversation in a chat channel — messages and the compose bar Pro tip The Q&A channel is usually the right place for questions about the material — that way other members benefit from the answer too. What's next Big updates and organized discussions happen in the feed , and live meetups — in events .

title: Take an exam and get your results
description: How to take a course exam, answer the questions, submit, and make sense of the results — including what happens if you don't pass
text: A course exam is a lesson like any other — it appears in the course structure, and sometimes you must pass it to move on to the next lesson. Here's how it works, from entry to results. 1 Enter the exam When you reach an exam-type lesson, an intro screen shows you everything you need to know upfront: the number of questions, the passing score, and whether there's a time limit. If the exam is a gate, you'll also see the message "You must pass the exam to move on to the next lesson". Ready? Click Start exam . The exam start screen — questions, passing score, and Start 2 Answer the questions Each question appears on its own, and you pick an answer with a click. At the top of the screen: A "Question X of Y" counter. Progress dots — one dot per question; an answered question fills in with color, and you can click a dot to jump to that question. A timer, if the instructor set a time limit. Move between questions with Previous and Next , and you can go back and change an answer before submitting. An exam question screen — counter, progress dots, and navigation 3 Submit After the last question, a submission confirmation window appears. Heads-up Once you click Submit , you can't go back into the exam and change answers. Make sure you've reviewed everything. 4 Get your results The results screen shows your score in a percentage ring, the number of correct answers, and the passing score. Passed? You'll see "Well done, you passed!" and the next lesson unlocks. Below that is a Question review — every question with your answer, and for the ones you got wrong, the correct answer too. An exam results screen — you passed 5 If you didn't pass No big deal. The results screen shows you exactly what to do: Lessons worth reviewing — recommended lessons tied to the questions you got wrong. The number of attempts you have left. Try again — for another attempt, or Back to the material to review the lessons first. An exam results screen — you didn't pass, recommendations, and another attempt What's next Passed all your exams and finished the course? My certificate is waiting for you.

title: My certificate
description: Getting your completion certificate — viewing it, downloading a PDF, and sharing on LinkedIn and WhatsApp
text: Finished the course or the training program? You've earned it. Your completion certificate is waiting in the platform — you can download it as a PDF, share it on social media, and keep it as a memento. 1 Open the certificate When you complete the program, the certificate screen opens with a personal congratulation ("Well done!") and a summary of what you accomplished. 2 What's on the certificate The certificate includes: The name of the program or course. Your name . A short description of what was completed (courses, lessons, and exams). The issue date and a serial number. The instructor's signature and a QR code. The student's completion certificate 3 Download and share Below the certificate are three buttons: Download PDF — a file to print or keep on record. Share on LinkedIn — an achievement like this deserves a post. Share on WhatsApp . The certificate's download and share buttons 4 Your journey in review At the bottom of the screen you'll find Your program summary — how many courses you completed, how many lessons and exams you passed, and how many learning hours you racked up. Pro tip The name on the certificate comes from your profile — if it needs fixing, update your profile in Settings before downloading. What's next Want to keep learning? Head back to My courses — a new course might be waiting there.

title: Chat with BOARDi inside your course
description: BOARDi — the learning assistant that answers questions from the course materials, with a jump to the exact moment in the lesson and summaries saved to your notes
headings: Get an answer with its source in the lesson
Save a summary to your notes
text: Got a question in the middle of a lesson? No need to wait for your instructor. BOARDi, WHITEBOARD's learning assistant, sits with you inside the course player and answers — but only from the course materials themselves. No guesses from the internet, just what your instructor actually taught. 1 Open BOARDi In the course player, click the BOARDi button on the side rail. A chat window opens — type your question in the Ask a question about the course... field and send. A chat with BOARDi in the course player — an answer with the source from the lesson 2 Get an answer with its source in the lesson BOARDi answers from the course content, and every answer comes with its source: a "From the material" chip with the lesson name and a timestamp (like "Lesson 2 · 03:17"). Click the chip and the player jumps to the exact moment the instructor explains it. Good to know BOARDi answers only from the course materials. If you ask about something that wasn't taught, it will say so explicitly — "outside the course material" — and if there's a relevant chapter in the course, it will point you to it. 3 Keep the conversation going Under every answer, BOARDi suggests a fitting follow-up question — click it to dig deeper, or write your own. Sometimes it will offer a few question directions to choose from. 4 Save a summary to your notes After a few questions, BOARDi will offer to save a summary of the conversation for you. Clicking Add summary to my notes writes the key points straight into your notes — including references to the timestamps mentioned in the chat. From there you can click Open in my notes to see the summary. The button to add the chat summary to My Notes Pro tip A good question for the end of every lesson: "Summarize the lesson so far". You get a tidy recap — and you can save it to your notes with one click. What's next The summaries BOARDi writes join your notes — how to manage them is covered in My notes — time-stamped notes .
